title: Rival humanoid maker lands $500M-plus chip-and-cloud strategic round by Q4 2026
body: Neura Robotics' Series C of up to $1.4 billion, which surfaced June 10 at a valuation reported near $7 billion, did more than set a robotics fundraising mark: it pulled Nvidia, Amazon, Qualcomm and Bosch directly onto a full-stack humanoid maker's cap table alongside a Tether-led syndicate. That roster signals chip and cloud strategics are now treating equity in humanoid builders as a way to anchor downstream demand for their compute, silicon and fleet-services stacks rather than waiting for arm's-length procurement. With deployment revenue across the humanoid sector still early and several rivals racing toward serial production, the prediction is that at least one other full-stack humanoid company closes a comparably large strategic round, $500 million or more, with at least one of the same chip or cloud strategics participating, by the fourth quarter of 2026.

reasoning.because: Neura Robotics drew a >=$1.4B strategic Series C from Nvidia, Amazon and Qualcomm on June 10
reasoning.given: Chip and cloud strategics now buy direct humanoid cap-table seats to lock compute and fleet demand
reasoning.so_that: A second full-stack humanoid maker closes a comparable round with at least one overlapping chip/cloud strategic
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026; another humanoid maker round >=$500M with a chip/cloud strategic
reasoning.plain_language: Investors that make AI chips and cloud just put big money into a robot maker, so another robot startup will get a similar deal soon.

summary: Neura Robotics' up-to-$1.4B Series C put Nvidia, Amazon and Qualcomm directly on a humanoid maker's cap table at a ~$7B valuation. That strategic pattern suggests another full-stack humanoid company will close a $500M-plus round with at least one overlapping chip or cloud backer by Q4 2026.
